entry.note: the caller's template=<dir> keyword (or a multi_options item '--template=<dir>') is forwarded unchanged through **kwargs to Repo._clone, where it becomes a git-clone option

guards.note: the clone option list Repo._clone hands to Git.check_unsafe_options, for Git._option_candidates([], kwargs) and for the shlex-split multi_options. The fix adds '--template', so template=, abbreviations such as templ=/--templ= and '--template <dir>' raise UnsafeOptionError before git.clone runs, unless allow_unsafe_options=True

sinks.note: git.clone(multi, '--', clone_url, clone_path, ..., **add_progress(kwargs, ...)) in Repo._clone reaches _call_process via Git.__getattr__. There transform_kwargs/transform_kwarg render template=<dir> as '--template=<dir>' and self.execute(call) starts 'git clone ... --template=<dir> -v -- <url> <path>' (safer_popen/Popen inside Git.execute, ~17 KB with overloads, too large for the slice). git copies <dir>/hooks into the new repository and runs its post-checkout hook during the clone

notes: Reviewed at 2.3 (second pass; re-verified in a third pass on 2026-09-28: guard behaviour re-run on the real functions from both blobs, git/cmd.py blob identical at both commits (5cba11f9), and git 2.55 ran a template post-checkout hook during a local clone). The clean slice keeps the fix's own comment above the new entry ('Can install hooks that execute during clone:'). The scrubber does not match it, it states git behaviour, and it appears in regression.diff as part of the inverted fix. It is the only per-entry comment left in unsafe_git_clone_options, because the older entries' comments were scrubbed. Option injection with OS command execution as the effect. Changed from the earlier draft: the sink stand-in moves from Repo._clone to Git._call_process, the in-slice direct caller of Git.execute, and Git.__getattr__/_call_process/execute_kwargs are added, so the git.clone dispatch is visible and transform_kwarg(s) are no longer orphaned. This matches the sibling clone events gitpython-2f96, gitpython-r9mr and gitpython-pr76. The scope label is unchanged because the true sink is Git.execute either way. To stay under the soft size limit, git/remote.py::add_progress is left out, as in those siblings. It is an identity passthrough: it returns the same kwargs dict, adding only progress=True when a progress object is given. Keeping it would put the clean slice at 24754 bytes, 178 over the soft limit. Regressed flow (e8d0fbf7): Repo.clone_from(url, to_path, template=<dir>) -> Repo._clone(**kwargs) -> Git._option_candidates([], kwargs) = ['--template'] -> Git.check_unsafe_options passes, because Repo.unsafe_git_clone_options is ['--upload-pack', '-u', '--config', '-c'] and neither the exact nor the prefix rule matches 'template'. The shlex-split multi_options token '--template=<dir>' likewise passes. -> git.clone(..., **add_progress(kwargs, git, progress)) -> Git.__getattr__ -> Git._call_process -> opts_kwargs (template is not in execute_kwargs) -> Git.transform_kwargs -> Git.transform_kwarg = ['--template=<dir>'] -> Git.execute (Popen). git then copies <dir>/hooks into the new .git and runs hooks/post-checkout at checkout. Clean (ffcb5359): the list gains '--template', so the canonical candidate 'template' matches exactly and UnsafeOptionError is raised before git.clone. Abbreviations are caught by the existing prefix rule in Git.check_unsafe_options. Verified concretely: I extracted the real Repo.unsafe_git_clone_options, Git._option_candidates, check_unsafe_options, _canonicalize_option_name, dashify and transform_kwarg(s) from both blobs and mirrored Repo._clone's two checks. Kwargs template=, templ= and templat=, and multi_options '--template=<dir>', '--template <dir>' and '--templ=<dir>', all pass at e8d0fbf7 and all raise at ffcb5359. Benign depth=1 and branch='main' with multi_options '--single-branch' pass at both. transform_kwargs(template=<dir>) returns ['--template=<dir>']. End to end with git 2.55: 'git clone -v --template=<dir> -- <local repo> <dst>', with an executable <dir>/hooks/post-checkout, ran the hook (marker file created). The fix touches only git/repo/base.py (the list entry, a comment and an attribute docstring the slicer drops) plus tests. git/cmd.py is byte-identical at both commits. Exploitation also needs a directory the attacker can stage, holding an executable hooks/post-checkout (advisory AC:H). The last hop, git running template hooks, is git behaviour outside the repo, as with --upload-pack in gitpython-2f96. Pair context: e8d0fbf7 (split single-char option values) is itself the clean commit of event gitpython-r9mr. Both commits came in through PR #2180. The regressed commit therefore already has the r9mr hardening, and the only difference between the pair is the '--template' entry. Parallel entries closed by the same list entry, not modelled: Repo.clone (instance method) and submodule cloning (Submodule._clone_repo -> Repo.clone_from). Not closed, and out of scope for this pair: Repo.init still forwards template= to git init unchecked at the clean commit. That is a separate advisory, GHSA-9rj7-rf2p-w77r, fixed later in d9ddb55b, and it is not in the slice. Dropped references accepted: Git.execute (true sink, too large); _AutoInterrupt and _CatFileContentStream (targets of the class-level TypeAlias assignments that are kept automatically); _GitMeta (Git's metaclass). None of these is on the modelled path except the true sink. Cross-file cuts the dropped-references check does not see: add_progress (above); Git.polish_url, Git.is_cygwin and Git.check_unsafe_protocols (URL/path handling, off the option flow); and handle_process_output, finalize_process, to_progress_instance and remove_password_if_present (after git has started). The tainted datum is a kwarg KEY (the option name) together with its value; taint engines that only propagate values may see <dir> reach argv but not the option name that makes it dangerous.
